description:
Why this issue exists: email/set.rs handle_email_set() returns a response with hardcoded 'oldState': '0' and 'newState': '0'. The caller in server.rs route_method does override these after the fact, but this creates a fragile two-step contract: any code path that returns early from handle_email_set (e.g. on validation error) will leak the hardcoded '0' values to clients. RFC 8621 §4.3 requires accurate old/new state on all responses including partial failures.

What needs to be done: Pass the current state into handle_email_set so it can embed the correct values directly, or have the function return a typed struct rather than a serde_json::Value blob so the caller cannot forget to patch it.
title: Email/set: create returns hardcoded oldState/newState 0 before caller override
